newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CHINA TO BUILD "DRAGON CITY" IN S.AFRICAN PROVINCE.
newsitem.headline: CHINA TO BUILD "DRAGON CITY" IN S.AFRICAN PROVINCE.

text.p: Chinese firms plan to build a "Dragon City" in South Africa's North West Province in a multi-billion dollar deal with foreign private investors, the province's premier Popo Molefe said on Thursday.
Molefe declined to name the financiers of the vast industrial park or the Chinese companies involved, but said the deal was worth more than $18 billion.
His comments at a press conference follow his earlier announcement of the deal in Beijing on Monday, which was met with scepticism from government and analysts.

"Any kind of investment like that would be most welcome and the department would do everything it could to make it possible, but we know nothing about it," Department of Trade and Industry spokesman Ismail Lagardien told Reuters on Wednesday.
Molefe emphasised that "Dragon City" was entirely a private sector initiative, although his provincial government would do all in its power to facilitate it.
The project would see China export about 500 factories lock, stock and barrel to a 4,430 hectare site adjoining the town of Potchefstroom, two hours' drive west of Johannesburg.
About 50,000 Chinese workers would populate the city, man light industries and impart skills to the local population.

Shortly after returning from a five-day official visit to Asia, Molefe told reporters that at least 130 Chinese companies had already signed letters of intent to move to South Africa and the land had already been purchased.
"This is not just a pipe dream. The piece of land has already been acquired," he said.
"I am reliably informed that the money is lying somewhere. Somewhere in Switzerland, the U.S. and possibly the U.K. I have been informed that contracts have been signed," he said.
Asked how the $18 billion figure had been calculated, Molefe said it included the transfer of machinery and equipment, the purchase of real estate and funds from overseas banks.
He said more information would be available once the full delegation returned from Tokyo on September 12.
Molefe's announcement coincides with a Taiwanese delegation to South Africa, eliciting criticism that China and Taiwan are waging a war for diplomatic recognition by South Africa.
Taiwan state television on Tuesday reported a plan to invest between $3 billion and $5 billion in a South African petrochemical development.
A spokesman for the Ministry of Mineral and Energy Affairs on Wednesday denied knowledge of the Taiwanese project.
Asked if his provincial government would welcome Taiwanese investment as well, Molefe said: "We want anyone to invest in our province who is engaged in legitimate business activities."

"Dragon City" would be developed over six years officially starting in November and would see the building of factories, warehouses, shopping malls, houses, schools and restaurants, as well as a hotel and a casino, Molefe said.
Ultimately the development would result in employment for almost half a million people, he added.
Apart from the Chinese project, Molefe's delegation had successfully created areas of conjunction with Indonesia and Singapore.
